question: What is the distinction between an SLA and an OLA?

choices.text: The SLA is a commitment to the customer, the OLA is an internal agreement between teams
The OLA only applies to Changes
The SLA only applies to Problems

explanation: The SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a time commitment generally made to the customer/business, while the OLA (Operational Level Agreement) is an equivalent agreement between internal teams.
pieges: Confusing the two terms which, although mechanically similar, have a different contractual scope.
